tool_flags.name: -sS
tool_flags.description: TCP SYN scan (stealth scan) — default scan type, sends SYN packets and waits for response

tool_flags.name: -sV
tool_flags.description: Service/version detection — probes open ports to determine service and version info

tool_flags.name: -O
tool_flags.description: Operating system detection — uses TCP/IP fingerprinting to guess the remote OS

tool_flags.name: -A
tool_flags.description: Aggressive scan — enables OS detection, version detection, script scanning, and traceroute

tool_flags.name: -sU
tool_flags.description: UDP scan — sends UDP packets to discover open UDP ports

tool_flags.name: -l
tool_flags.description: Listen mode — binds and listens for inbound connections

tool_flags.name: -v
tool_flags.description: Verbose output — provides more detailed connection information

tool_flags.name: -e
tool_flags.description: Execute — runs a program after connecting or listening (security risk)

tool_flags.name: -z
tool_flags.description: Zero-I/O mode — scans ports without sending any data (used for port scanning)

tool_flags.name: --dump
tool_flags.description: Dump the entire database contents or specific tables

tool_flags.name: --batch
tool_flags.description: Run in non-interactive mode — use default options for all prompts

tool_flags.name: --random-agent
tool_flags.description: Use a randomly selected User-Agent header to avoid fingerprinting

tool_flags.name: --level
tool_flags.description: Level of tests to perform (1-5), higher levels include more payloads and headers

tool_flags.name: -q
tool_flags.description: Quiet mode — suppresses banner and startup messages

tool_flags.name: -r
tool_flags.description: Run resource file — execute msfconsole commands from a script file

tool_flags.name: -x
tool_flags.description: Execute command — runs a specific msfconsole command and exits

tool_flags.name: -l
tool_flags.description: Single username to try (no bruteforce for username)

tool_flags.name: -P
tool_flags.description: Password file — path to a file containing passwords to try

tool_flags.name: -t
tool_flags.description: Number of parallel threads/tasks to use (default: 16)

tool_flags.name: -f
tool_flags.description: Exit on first success — stops cracking when a valid password is found

tool_flags.name: -w
tool_flags.description: Wordlist file — path to dictionary file for WPA/WPA2 PSK cracking

tool_flags.name: -b
tool_flags.description: BSSID filter — target a specific access point by its MAC address

tool_flags.name: -K
tool_flags.description: KoreK attack — use KoreK attacks for WEP cracking (faster)

tool_flags.name: -i
tool_flags.description: Capture interface — specify which network interface to capture from

tool_flags.name: -k
tool_flags.description: Start capturing immediately — begins live capture on startup

tool_flags.name: -Y
tool_flags.description: Display filter — apply a display filter on startup (e.g., "http" or "tcp.port==80")

tool_flags.name: -r
tool_flags.description: Read capture file — open and analyze an existing pcap/pcapng file

tool_flags.name: --wordlist
tool_flags.description: Dictionary attack mode — use a wordlist file for password cracking

tool_flags.name: --incremental
tool_flags.description: Brute force mode — try all possible character combinations

tool_flags.name: --format
tool_flags.description: Hash format — specify the hash type (e.g., "raw-md5", "ntlm", "sha512crypt")

tool_flags.name: --show
tool_flags.description: Show cracked passwords — display passwords that have already been cracked
